name: Volvo
overview: Renowned worldwide for safety innovation and in Australia for local assembly of the 140/240 series, Bathurst-winning touring cars, and rapid transition to electrified SUVs.
australian_history: Volvo began selling in Australia in the 1960s and established Volvo Australia Pty Ltd in 1970. Between 1970 and 1989, Volvo passenger cars—including the 144, 164, 240, and 264—were assembled in Australia, first at Motor Producers Limited (Clayton, VIC) and later at Volvo's dedicated assembly plant in Wacol, Brisbane (QLD). The robust 240 series became an indelible part of Australian family life. Volvo also etched its name into Australian motorsport folklore: Robbie Francevic won the 1986 Australian Touring Car Championship in an Australian-developed Volvo 240 Turbo ('The Flying Brick'), and Jim Richards and Rickard Rydell famously won the 1998 AMP Bathurst 1000 in an S40 Super Tourer. Today, Volvo Car Australia is headquartered in Sydney and is leading the brand's global charge toward full electrification with the XC40/EX40, EX30, and XC90.

models.name: 240 & 850 Series
models.overview: The twin legends that transformed Volvo's reputation in Australia. The 240 Series was assembled locally at Clayton, Victoria, setting world safety standards and winning the 1986 Australian Touring Car Championship as the 'Flying Brick'. Its successor, the 850 Series, introduced front-wheel drive transverse 5-cylinder performance, celebrated by the limited-edition 850 T-5R and the 850 Super Tourers raced by Peter Brock and Jim Richards.

240-850.name: 240 & 850 Series
240-850.overview: The twin legends that transformed Volvo's reputation in Australia. The 240 Series was assembled locally at Clayton, Victoria, setting world safety standards and winning the 1986 Australian Touring Car Championship as the 'Flying Brick'. Its successor, the 850 Series, introduced front-wheel drive transverse 5-cylinder performance, celebrated by the limited-edition 850 T-5R and the 850 Super Tourers raced by Peter Brock and Jim Richards.
240-850.australian_market_notes: Locally assembled at Clayton, Victoria by Volvo Australia from 1975 to 1988. In 1986, Kiwi driver Robbie Francevic drove the Mark Petch/Volvo Dealer Team 240 Turbo to outright victory in the Australian Touring Car Championship—the first and only turbo Volvo to win the ATCC. A decade later in 1996, Peter Brock and Jim Richards famously piloted factory Volvo 850 sedans in the Australian Super Touring Championship and Bathurst 1000.
